title: Constant module inverse image from a constant underlying set inverse image
statement: Let f:X -> U be a morphism of schemes, with X nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and let R be a commutative ring in Type (u+1). Let F be a sheaf of R-modules on the small etale site of U [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. If the set inverse image f^{-1} of the underlying sheaf of sets of F is constant on X [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], then the module inverse image f^*F [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is constant as an R-module sheaf. No finiteness assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 0DV5, proof of (2)--(3), Tag 0DV6; sites-modules Tag 093S; agent elaboration to arbitrary constant values using connectedness

proof.text: Module inverse image commutes with passage to underlying sets: neighbourhood colimits are filtered, and forgetting modules preserves their colimits and finite limits, hence commutes with sheafification. Thus the underlying sheaf of f^*F is constant.

On a connected nonempty scheme the global sections of a constant set sheaf are its value, since locally constant functions are constant. Thus the constant set sheaf functor is fully faithful and preserves finite products. Transfer addition, zero, negation, and each scalar action to the value. Faithfulness gives the module axioms, and the underlying identification is then a module-sheaf isomorphism. Equivalently, use reflection of isomorphisms on the constant/global-sections counit. This applies to the zero module, zero coefficient ring, and infinite constant values.
